answer: Admission is gated by a priced time-lock escrow: opening an agent identity freezes 40 verified task-hours, released only after work is attested across five later epochs. The escrow forms a reef across every inlet of new entrants - one full bond per public key, so n puppets each pay the full clock with no batch discount, while an honest user pays once. The registry prisms each key's history into per-epoch attestations, so a clone cannot inherit, split, or reset a lock; re-keying restarts the timer. Marginal attacker cost therefore grows linearly with fleet size.
